title: The other value-free four-place laws build equality and are NP-complete
claim: The not-exactly-two and twelve classes build equality on 4-regular pieces, so deciding them on 4-regular systems is NP-complete and their failures are coNP-complete to recognise. Each class has a piece with five internal points of degree 4, four ports of degree 1 and six lines without repetition, whose accepted port relation is (a = b) x {0,1}^2: two ports forced equal, two free. Regularization: replace each variable with occurrence count d by m = max(d, 2) copies joined in a cycle by m equality pieces; the 2m free ports fill the copies' 2m - d spare incidences, and the remaining sum of d, four per constraint, fill one absorber point per constraint. The result is a simple 4-regular 4-uniform system without repeated lines, solvable iff the instance is. With Schaefer's theorem (neither class is 0-valid, 1-valid, Horn, dual Horn, bijunctive or affine) both are NP-complete on 4-regular systems. Checked: the pieces by enumeration, the reduction end to end on random instances with a SAT solver.
failure_conditions: A piece whose accepted relation is not (a = b) x {0,1}^2.
A regularized system that is not 4-regular, not simple, has a repeated line, or differs in satisfiability from its source.
Either class closed under a Schaefer polymorphism.
foundation_claim_scope: Decision complexity of two value-free laws on regular systems; no counting claim.

validation.independence: Written by Claude in one session at the repository owner's request on 2026-10-31.
validation.status: checked: the equality pieces by enumeration (structures up to five internal points); Schaefer polymorphisms; the regularization on random instances against a SAT solver; no human or external review
validation.novelty: Bounded-occurrence hardness via equality gadgets is classical (Tovey; Dalmau-Ford with constants); here the laws cannot pin, so equality is built without constants. The pieces are new (explicit).
